sop:
Please set up a daily reminder automation to send out emails to our members reminding them of their upcoming renewal date. This should start at 11:00 AM every day, and we want to send a reminder to everyone whose renewal date is tomorrow and who are currently active members. The email should say: "Hi [Member Name], a reminder from the gym: your renewal date is tomorrow."

Please ensure that no more than 30 emails are sent in a batch, and that these emails only go out between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM. If the batch needs to be sent, I will approve it within 1 hour and review up to 5 previews before approving. No one should receive more than 150 messages per day. Let everyone know if the batch isn't approved so we can adjust accordingly.
policy:
policy GymPolicy {
  allow read Members(name, email, renews_on, status, health_notes)
  allow contact Members.email
  deny reveal Members.health_notes
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
  approval batch valid 1 hour max 30 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Members "Members" { name: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, health_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure GymRenewalDateReminders {
  about "Remind each member about their renewal date"
  policy GymPolicy
  sheet Members "Members" { name: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, health_notes: Text private }
  trigger every day at 11:00

  let all = fetch Members
  let due = filter all where renews_on == today() + 1 day and status == "active"
  let msgs = draft each r in due up to 30 email to r.email subject "Your renewal date tomorrow": "Hi {r.name}, a reminder from the gym: your renewal date is tomorrow."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 1 day else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

procedure ClinicFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new patient, then follow up once"
  policy ClinicPolicy
  sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Visits

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.patient}, thanks for choosing the clinic! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Visits
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.patient default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

Only the owner should be able to approve sending these reminders, and the owner has one day to give approval. The reminder should say, "Hi [Patient Name], it’s been a while! We’d love to see you again at the clinic." No more than 15 reminders should be sent each day, and this process can only run between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM. policy:
policy ClinicPolicy {
  allow read Visits(patient, phone, starts, status, diagnosis)
  allow contact Visits.phone
  deny reveal Visits.diagnosis
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 15 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
program:
procedure ClinicWinBack {
  about "Nudge patients whose appointment was long ago"
  policy ClinicPolicy
  sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
  trigger every tuesday at 08:30

  let all = fetch Visits
  let old = filter all where days_between(starts, today()) >= 60 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by starts first 15
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 15 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.patient default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the clinic."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 1 day else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

program:
procedure RetailFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy RetailPolicy
  sheet Orders "Orders" { customer: Text, email: Email, ordered_on: Date, status: Text, total: Money, card_note: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Orders

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the shop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Orders
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "shipped" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

- I only need 200 messages sent per day.

Thanks!

policy PestPolicy {
  allow read Treatments(customer, phone, status, pet_notes)
  allow write Treatments(status)
  allow contact Treatments.phone
  deny reveal Treatments.pet_notes
  limit sends 200 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
}
sheets: sheet Treatments "Treatments" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, treat_on: Date, status: Text, price: Money, pet_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure PestFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy PestPolicy
  sheet Treatments "Treatments" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, treat_on: Date, status: Text, price: Money, pet_notes: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Treatments

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the company! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 1 day else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Treatments
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.customer}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 1 day else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

}

Only send these reminders between 9 AM and 9 PM, and limit the number of messages to 20 per day. No more than 20 previews should be allowed at any time, with each batch needing approval within one hour. If the batch isn't approved within six hours, the process should stop.   allow read Jobs(customer, email, due, status)
  allow contact Jobs.email
  deny reveal Jobs.file_link
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
  approval batch valid 1 hour max 20 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Jobs "Jobs" { customer: Text, email: Email, due: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, file_link: Text private }
program:
procedure PrintshopWinBack {
  about "Nudge customers whose print job was long ago"
  policy PrintshopPolicy
  sheet Jobs "Jobs" { customer: Text, email: Email, due: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, file_link: Text private }
  trigger every friday at 08:00

  let all = fetch Jobs
  let old = filter all where days_between(due, today()) >= 30 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by due first 20
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 20 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop:
Hey there,

Could you set up an automation that nudges clients whose cleaning was over 90 days ago? It should happen daily at 10 AM. The system should check for all cleanings, find those older than 90 days and not marked as cancelled, then select the first 15. For each of these, send them a text like this: "Hi [Client Name], it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the service."

Make sure to get my approval before sending out these nudges. Only allow up to 15 texts per batch and ensure they're sent between 9 AM and 9 PM. If I don’t approve a batch within 6 hours, please stop the process.

Thanks!
policy:
policy CleaningPolicy {
  allow read Cleanings(client, phone, scheduled, status, door_code)
  allow contact Cleanings.phone
  deny reveal Cleanings.door_code
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 15 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Cleanings "Cleanings" { client: Text, phone: Phone, scheduled: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, door_code: Text private }
program:
procedure CleaningWinBack {
  about "Nudge clients whose cleaning was long ago"
  policy CleaningPolicy
  sheet Cleanings "Cleanings" { client: Text, phone: Phone, scheduled: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, door_code: Text private }
  trigger every day at 10:00

  let all = fetch Cleanings
  let old = filter all where days_between(scheduled, today()) >= 90 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by scheduled first 15
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 15 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.client}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the service."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

program:
procedure DentalWinBack {
  about "Nudge patients whose cleaning was long ago"
  policy DentalPolicy
  sheet Patients "Patients" { name: Text, mobile: Phone, next_visit: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, medical_history: Text private }
  trigger every monday at 09:00

  let all = fetch Patients
  let old = filter all where days_between(next_visit, today()) >= 60 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by next_visit first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 sms to r.mobile: "Hi {r.name}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the office."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

- Wait 2 days before sending a follow-up message asking, "Hi [Client Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" This message needs to be approved by me within 2 hours as well.

- Only send messages on weekdays.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

  allow contact Cleanings.phone

program:
procedure CleaningFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new client, then follow up once"
  policy CleaningPolicy
  sheet Cleanings "Cleanings" { client: Text, phone: Phone, scheduled: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, door_code: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Cleanings

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.client}, thanks for choosing the service! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Cleanings
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.client default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  allow read Jobs(owner_name, phone, status, vin)
  allow write Jobs(status)
  allow contact Jobs.phone

}

program:
procedure AutorepairFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy AutorepairPolicy
  sheet Jobs "Jobs" { owner_name: Text, phone: Phone, promised: DateTime, status: Text, estimate: Money, vin: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Jobs

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.owner_name default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the shop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch Jobs
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "ready" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.owner_name default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

Could you please set up an automation to follow up with new swimmers? Here are the details:

- When a new swimmer is added to the "SwimPasses" sheet, send them a welcome email.
- Wait 3 days and then send a follow-up email asking if they need any help.
- Only send these emails during business hours (from 7:30 AM to 7:00 PM).
- The owner must approve both emails before they are sent.
- No more than 150 emails can be sent in a single day.
- The owner should have one day to approve each email.

Thanks!
policy:
policy PoolPolicy {
  allow read SwimPasses(swimmer, email, status, health_flags)
  allow write SwimPasses(status)
  allow contact SwimPasses.email
  deny reveal SwimPasses.health_flags
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
}
sheets: sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
program:
procedure PoolFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new swimmer, then follow up once"
  policy PoolPolicy
  sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in SwimPasses

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.swimmer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the pool! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 1 day else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch SwimPasses
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "expired" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.swimmer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 1 day else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

procedure RetailFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy RetailPolicy
  sheet Orders "Orders" { customer: Text, email: Email, ordered_on: Date, status: Text, total: Money, card_note: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Orders

}

}

sop:
Please review and approve the following automation steps for customer follow-ups:

1. When a new cake order is placed, send an initial welcome email to the customer.
   - Subject: "Hi [Customer Name], thanks for choosing the bakery! Reply with any questions."
2. Wait 3 days after sending the first email.
3. If the status hasn't been updated to "confirmed" or "cancelled," send a follow-up check-in email.
   - Subject: "Hi [Customer Name, default to 'there'], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"

Please approve both emails by tomorrow morning at 8 AM. Thank you!
policy:
policy BakeryPolicy {
  allow read CakeOrders(customer, email, status, address)
  allow write CakeOrders(status)
  allow contact CakeOrders.email
  deny reveal CakeOrders.address
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
}
sheets: sheet CakeOrders "CakeOrders" { customer: Text, email: Email, pickup: Date, status: Text, price: Money, address: Text private }
program:
procedure BakeryFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy BakeryPolicy
  sheet CakeOrders "CakeOrders" { customer: Text, email: Email, pickup: Date, status: Text, price: Money, address: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in CakeOrders

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.customer}, thanks for choosing the bakery! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 1 day else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch CakeOrders
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "confirmed" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 1 day else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  sheet Leagues "Leagues" { bowler: Text, phone: Phone, next_game: DateTime, status: Text, dues: Money, shoe_size_notes: Text private }

  send ok
}

program:
procedure PetgroomerFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new pet owner, then follow up once"
  policy PetgroomerPolicy
  sheet Grooms "Grooms" { owner: Text, phone: Phone, appointment: DateTime, status: Text, price: Money, behavior_notes: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Grooms

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.owner default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the salon! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 7 days
  let all = fetch Grooms
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.owner}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

- Wait 5 days before sending a follow-up check-in email.

- Limit the daily number of emails to 150.

Thank you!

  allow read Skaters(skater, email, status)
  allow write Skaters(status)
  allow contact Skaters.email
  deny reveal Skaters.medical_info
  limit sends 150 per day

}

program:
procedure IcerinkFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new skater, then follow up once"
  policy IcerinkPolicy
  sheet Skaters "Skaters" { skater: Text, email: Email, session_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, medical_info: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Skaters

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.skater default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the rink! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Skaters
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "skated" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.skater default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop: Could you please set up an automation to nudge surfers whose lesson was over 90 days ago? It should happen every Tuesday at 8 AM. policy SurfPolicy {
  allow read Lessons(surfer, phone, lesson_at, status, swim_level)
  allow contact Lessons.phone
  deny reveal Lessons.swim_level

  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 10 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Lessons "Lessons" { surfer: Text, phone: Phone, lesson_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, swim_level: Text private }
program:
procedure SurfWinBack {
  about "Nudge surfers whose surf lesson was long ago"
  policy SurfPolicy
  sheet Lessons "Lessons" { surfer: Text, phone: Phone, lesson_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, swim_level: Text private }
  trigger every tuesday at 08:00

  let all = fetch Lessons
  let old = filter all where days_between(lesson_at, today()) >= 90 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by lesson_at first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.surfer default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the school."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 1 day else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop:
Could you please set up an automation to nudge renters who haven't returned their costumes for a long time? The automation should:

- Check every day at 4:00 PM.
- Only contact those who are overdue by more than 42 days and whose status isn't cancelled.
- Draft up to 15 SMS messages like this: "Hi [renter name or there], it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
- Ask for my approval to send these messages within a 30-minute window with a maximum of 15 previews.
- Only allow 200 messages to be sent per day and between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM.
- Ensure no one's ID number is revealed.

Thank you!
policy:
policy CostumePolicy {
  allow read Rentals(renter, phone, due_back, status)
  allow contact Rentals.phone
  deny reveal Rentals.id_number
  limit sends 200 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
  approval batch valid 30 minutes max 15 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Rentals "Rentals" { renter: Text, phone: Phone, due_back: Date, status: Text, deposit: Money, id_number: Text private }
program:
procedure CostumeWinBack {
  about "Nudge renters whose return date was long ago"
  policy CostumePolicy
  sheet Rentals "Rentals" { renter: Text, phone: Phone, due_back: Date, status: Text, deposit: Money, id_number: Text private }
  trigger every day at 16:00

  let all = fetch Rentals
  let old = filter all where days_between(due_back, today()) >= 42 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by due_back first 15
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 15 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.renter default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

program:
procedure PoolFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new swimmer, then follow up once"
  policy PoolPolicy
  sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in SwimPasses

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.swimmer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the pool! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch SwimPasses
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "expired" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.swimmer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
  notify owner "Please update my business partner yourself."
}

sop:
Please create an automation for following up with new patients after their first visit. The automation should:

- Send an initial message saying "Hi [Patient Name], thanks for choosing our office! Reply with any questions." within two hours of a new patient being added to the Patients sheet. Only I should be able to approve or reject this message.
- Wait five days before sending a follow-up message saying "Hi [Patient Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" Only I should be able to approve or reject this message too.
- Ensure no more than 150 messages are sent in a day and only between 8 AM and 8 PM.
- Do not share any sensitive information like medical history.

Let me know if you have any questions!
policy:
policy DentalPolicy {
  allow read Patients(name, mobile, status, medical_history)
  allow write Patients(status)
  allow contact Patients.mobile
  deny reveal Patients.medical_history
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
}
sheets: sheet Patients "Patients" { name: Text, mobile: Phone, next_visit: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, medical_history: Text private }
program:
procedure DentalFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new patient, then follow up once"
  policy DentalPolicy
  sheet Patients "Patients" { name: Text, mobile: Phone, next_visit: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, medical_history: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Patients

  let first = draft sms to r.mobile: "Hi {r.name}, thanks for choosing the office! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Patients
  let now_r = find all where mobile == r.mobile else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.mobile: "Hi {now_r.name default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

Also, make sure these messages are sent between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM. Please approve batches of up to 20 messages at a time and allow for a preview of 5 messages before sending.   allow read Visits(patient, phone, starts, status)
  allow contact Visits.phone
  deny reveal Visits.diagnosis
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 20 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
program:
procedure ClinicWinBack {
  about "Nudge patients whose appointment was long ago"
  policy ClinicPolicy
  sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
  trigger every day at 10:00

  let all = fetch Visits
  let old = filter all where days_between(starts, today()) >= 60 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by starts first 20
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 20 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.patient default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the clinic."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop: Could you please set up an automation for our restaurant follow-up process? It should send a confirmation message to a guest right after their booking is made, and then check back with them two days later to see how everything is going. The owner needs to approve the initial message within 2 hours; if not, the automation should stop. If the guest has been seated or the booking is cancelled, it should stop the follow-up process. Additionally, the follow-up message should be sent with the owner's approval within 2 hours. The system should only send these messages between 8 AM and 8 PM, and no more than 150 messages per day. Please make sure the guest's information remains private, especially their dietary allergies.
policy:
policy RestaurantPolicy {
  allow read Bookings(guest, phone, status)
  allow write Bookings(status)
  allow contact Bookings.phone
  deny reveal Bookings.allergies
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
}
sheets: sheet Bookings "Bookings" { guest: Text, phone: Phone, at: DateTime, status: Text, deposit: Money, allergies: Text private }
program:
procedure RestaurantFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new guest, then follow up once"
  policy RestaurantPolicy
  sheet Bookings "Bookings" { guest: Text, phone: Phone, at: DateTime, status: Text, deposit: Money, allergies: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Bookings

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.guest}, thanks for choosing the restaurant! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Bookings
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "seated" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.guest}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

program:
procedure PrintshopFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy PrintshopPolicy
  sheet Jobs "Jobs" { customer: Text, email: Email, due: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, file_link: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Jobs

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the shop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Jobs
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "printed" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.customer}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

procedure RetailWinBack {
  about "Nudge customers whose order was long ago"
  policy RetailPolicy
  sheet Orders "Orders" { customer: Text, email: Email, ordered_on: Date, status: Text, total: Money, card_note: Text private }
  trigger every day at 10:00

  let all = fetch Orders
  let old = filter all where days_between(ordered_on, today()) >= 30 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by ordered_on first 20
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 20 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop: Please set up an automation to nudge fencers who haven't participated in a bout for over 90 days. The automation should run every Wednesday at 9:00 AM and only send emails between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM. It should send up to 10 emails per day, with a maximum of 10 emails in one batch. The approval for the batch should be requested within one hour and a preview of 5 emails is allowed. If the batch isn't approved within 12 hours, the process should stop.   allow read Fencers(fencer, email, bout_at, status, injury_notes)
  allow contact Fencers.email
  deny reveal Fencers.injury_notes
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00

sheets: sheet Fencers "Fencers" { fencer: Text, email: Email, bout_at: DateTime, status: Text, dues: Money, injury_notes: Text private }

}

sop:
Please set up an automation to follow up with new swimmers after they've purchased passes. Here are the details:

- When a new row is added to the "SwimPasses" sheet, send a welcome email to the swimmer. Ensure the email says: "Hi [Swimmer Name], thanks for choosing the pool! Reply with any questions."
- Wait 5 days, then send a check-in email to the same swimmer asking, "Hi [Swimmer Name (default to there if name is missing)], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
- Only the owner should approve these emails before they're sent.
- Only send these emails between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM.
- Limit the number of emails sent to 100 per day.
- Include the private health flags in both emails, but don’t show them in plain text.

Thanks!
policy:
policy PoolPolicy {
  allow read SwimPasses(swimmer, email, status, health_flags)
  allow write SwimPasses(status)
  allow contact SwimPasses.email
  deny reveal SwimPasses.health_flags
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
}
sheets: sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
program:
procedure PoolFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new swimmer, then follow up once"
  policy PoolPolicy
  sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in SwimPasses

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.swimmer}, thanks for choosing the pool! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch SwimPasses
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "expired" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.swimmer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

program:
procedure LandscapingFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy LandscapingPolicy
  sheet Quotes "Quotes" { customer: Text, email: Email, sent_on: Date, status: Text, amount: Money, gate_code: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Quotes

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.customer}, thanks for choosing the company! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 7 days
  let all = fetch Quotes
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "sent" or now_r.status == "declined" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

program:
procedure BookstoreWinBack {
  about "Nudge customers whose hold was long ago"
  policy BookstorePolicy
  sheet Holds "Holds" { customer: Text, email: Email, held_until: Date, status: Text, prepaid: Money, phone_note: Text private }
  trigger every day at 09:00

  let all = fetch Holds
  let old = filter all where days_between(held_until, today()) >= 60 and status != "expired"
  let oldest = sort old by held_until first 20
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 20 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.customer}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the store."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop: Could you please set up an automation to nudge customers whose watch repairs have been completed for over 42 days and haven't been cancelled? This should happen daily at 4:00 PM. We want to send a friendly reminder to these customers through email. Only send up to 10 emails a day, and only between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM. Each group of reminders needs to be reviewed within 2 hours, and we can preview up to 5 at a time before final approval. Let me know if this works for you.
policy:
policy WatchesPolicy {
  allow read Watches(owner, email, ready_on, status, serial_number)
  allow contact Watches.email
  deny reveal Watches.serial_number
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 10 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Watches "Watches" { owner: Text, email: Email, ready_on: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, serial_number: Text private }
program:
procedure WatchesWinBack {
  about "Nudge owners whose watch repair was long ago"
  policy WatchesPolicy
  sheet Watches "Watches" { owner: Text, email: Email, ready_on: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, serial_number: Text private }
  trigger every day at 16:00

  let all = fetch Watches
  let old = filter all where days_between(ready_on, today()) >= 42 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by ready_on first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.owner default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 1 day else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

Could you please set up an automation to handle customer follow-ups after they've submitted a repair request? Here are the details:

- When a new repair request is created:

  - Wait 2 days.
  - Then send a follow-up message saying "Hi [Customer Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" (Only send this message once.)

Make sure both messages get approved by me before sending. The follow-up message should only be sent if the status hasn’t changed to "ready" or "cancelled" during the waiting period.

Also, ensure these messages are sent between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM, and no more than 200 messages per day.

Thank you!
policy:
policy BikeshopPolicy {
  allow read Repairs(customer, phone, status, lock_code)
  allow write Repairs(status)
  allow contact Repairs.phone
  deny reveal Repairs.lock_code
  limit sends 200 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
}
sheets: sheet Repairs "Repairs" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, ready_on: Date, status: Text, estimate: Money, lock_code: Text private }
program:
procedure BikeshopFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy BikeshopPolicy
  sheet Repairs "Repairs" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, ready_on: Date, status: Text, estimate: Money, lock_code: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Repairs

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.customer}, thanks for choosing the shop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Repairs
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "ready" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

- Send this message to the client’s phone number.
- Update the status to "contacted".
- Wait 5 days before sending a follow-up message asking, "Hi [client name] (or default to there), just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" and again get approval within 6 hours.

  allow read Repairs(client, phone, status)
  allow write Repairs(status)
  allow contact Repairs.phone
  deny reveal Repairs.address
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
}
sheets: sheet Repairs "Repairs" { client: Text, phone: Phone, promised_on: Date, status: Text, estimate: Money, address: Text private }
program:
procedure FurnitureFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new client, then follow up once"
  policy FurniturePolicy
  sheet Repairs "Repairs" { client: Text, phone: Phone, promised_on: Date, status: Text, estimate: Money, address: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Repairs

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.client}, thanks for choosing the workshop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Repairs
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "ready" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.client default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  allow read CakeOrders(customer, email, pickup, status)
  allow contact CakeOrders.email
  deny reveal CakeOrders.address
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00

}
sheets: sheet CakeOrders "CakeOrders" { customer: Text, email: Email, pickup: Date, status: Text, price: Money, address: Text private }
program:
procedure BakeryPickupDateReminders {
  about "Remind each customer about their pickup date"
  policy BakeryPolicy
  sheet CakeOrders "CakeOrders" { customer: Text, email: Email, pickup: Date, status: Text, price: Money, address: Text private }
  trigger every monday at 08:00

  let due = filter all where pickup == today() + 7 days and status == "new"
  let msgs = draft each r in due up to 30 email to r.email subject "Your pickup date in a week": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, a reminder from the bakery: your pickup date is in a week."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

  sheet Makers "Makers" { maker: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, door_pin: Text private }

  trigger when new row r in Visits

  update r set status = "contacted"

  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.patient default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop: Please create an automated reminder system that emails our customers when their print jobs are queued for three days from today. This should happen every Monday at 11:00 AM. The email should be sent to the customer's contact email and include a reminder that their job will be printed in three days. Only the first 50 reminders should be approved each week, and we should not exceed sending more than 100 emails per day. Please ensure these emails are sent between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM. Also, set a timeout of 6 hours for approving the batch; if it’s not approved within that time, stop the process. Thank you!
policy:
policy PrintshopPolicy {
  allow read Jobs(customer, email, due, status)
  allow contact Jobs.email
  deny reveal Jobs.file_link
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
  approval batch valid 30 minutes max 50 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Jobs "Jobs" { customer: Text, email: Email, due: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, file_link: Text private }
program:
procedure PrintshopPrintJobReminders {
  about "Remind each customer about their print job"
  policy PrintshopPolicy
  sheet Jobs "Jobs" { customer: Text, email: Email, due: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, file_link: Text private }
  trigger every monday at 11:00

  let all = fetch Jobs
  let due = filter all where due == today() + 3 days and status == "queued"
  let msgs = draft each r in due up to 50 email to r.email subject "Your print job in three days": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, a reminder from the shop: your print job is in three days."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop:
Please set up an automation to follow up with new students after they sign up. Here are the details:

- When a new student is added to the Lessons sheet, send the first message: "Hi [Student Name], thanks for choosing the school! Reply with any questions." This message should be reviewed by me within 6 hours.
- Wait 3 days after sending the first message.
- Then send a follow-up message: "Hi [Student Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" This message also needs my review within 6 hours.
- Limit the number of messages sent per day to 100.
- Only send messages during business hours, from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM.
- Make sure not to share notes on student progress in either message.

Thank you!
policy:
policy MusicPolicy {
  allow read Lessons(student, parent_phone, status, progress_notes)
  allow write Lessons(status)
  allow contact Lessons.parent_phone
  deny reveal Lessons.progress_notes
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
}
sheets: sheet Lessons "Lessons" { student: Text, parent_phone: Phone, lesson_at: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, progress_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure MusicFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new student, then follow up once"
  policy MusicPolicy
  sheet Lessons "Lessons" { student: Text, parent_phone: Phone, lesson_at: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, progress_notes: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Lessons

  let first = draft sms to r.parent_phone: "Hi {r.student default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the school! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch Lessons
  let now_r = find all where parent_phone == r.parent_phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.parent_phone: "Hi {now_r.student}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  about "Contact a new host, then follow up once"
  policy LasertagPolicy
  sheet Parties "Parties" { host: Text, phone: Phone, party_at: DateTime, status: Text, deposit: Money, kid_allergies: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Parties

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.host}, thanks for choosing the arena! Reply with any questions."

  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Parties
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "played" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.host}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 1 day else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
  notify owner "Please update our bookkeeper yourself."
}

sop: Please create an automation to contact our new readers after they've placed an order. The process should involve sending an initial welcome email, then following up after 5 days if they haven't contacted us. Only the owner should approve the messages. If the status changes to "held" or "cancelled," the process should stop. The automation should send emails between 9 AM and 9 PM daily, and no more than 50 emails per day. Please ensure both emails are approved before sending.
policy:
policy ComicsPolicy {
  allow read PullList(reader, email, status, home_address)
  allow write PullList(status)
  allow contact PullList.email
  deny reveal PullList.home_address
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
}
sheets: sheet PullList "PullList" { reader: Text, email: Email, arrives_on: Date, status: Text, owed: Money, home_address: Text private }
program:
procedure ComicsFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new reader, then follow up once"
  policy ComicsPolicy
  sheet PullList "PullList" { reader: Text, email: Email, arrives_on: Date, status: Text, owed: Money, home_address: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in PullList

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.reader default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the shop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 1 day else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch PullList
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "held" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.reader default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 1 day else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

We'd like these nudges to happen daily at 8:00 AM. Only the top 20 oldest cases should be contacted each day. Each message should say, "Hi [Customer Name], it's been a while! We’d love to see you again at the shop." Please get my approval before sending any messages, and ensure this happens no more than 6 hours after drafting the message. No messages should be sent outside of business hours (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM). Limit the total number of messages sent to 100 per day.
policy:
policy BikeshopPolicy {
  allow read Repairs(customer, phone, ready_on, status)
  allow contact Repairs.phone
  deny reveal Repairs.lock_code
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
}
sheets: sheet Repairs "Repairs" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, ready_on: Date, status: Text, estimate: Money, lock_code: Text private }

sop:
Please set up an automation to handle refund requests according to the following rules:

- Refunds are only allowed for requests made within the last 14 days. If a request is older than 14 days, please notify me so I can take appropriate action.
- No single refund can exceed $75. If a request is for more than $75, please review it before proceeding.
- For refunds up to $10, they can be processed automatically. For larger amounts, I need to approve the refund.
- Only three messages can be sent daily, and this must be done between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM.
- All messages should be sent directly to the customer's mobile number provided in the request.

Thank you!
policy:
policy DentalRefundPolicy {
  allow read RefundRequests(request_id, name, mobile, amount, purchased)
  allow write RefundRequests(status)
  allow contact RefundRequests.mobile
  limit refund $75 per action
  limit refund $225 per day
  refund without approval up to $10
  limit sends 30 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
}
sheets: sheet RefundRequests "RefundRequests" { request_id: Text, name: Text, mobile: Phone, amount: Money, purchased: Date, status: Text }
